ROBOTS: https://seletti.it/robots.txt fetched FIRST, before any other request on the host (HTTP 200, 3622 bytes, profile safari15_5). Standard Shopify storefront file. A regex sweep of the FULL text for 'claude' and 'anthropic' returns ZERO matches - no 'User-agent: ClaudeBot', no 'anthropic-ai', no 'Claude-Web', no Content-Signal line. Two groups only: 'User-agent: *' (Allow: / plus private/transactional Disallows - /admin, /cart/, /checkout, /checkouts/, /orders, /account, /services, /sf_*, /79959327067, /cdn/wpm/*.js, /cart.js, /recommendations/products) and 'User-agent: adsbot-google'. Crawl traps disallowed under '*': '/collections/*sort_by*', '/collections/*+*', '/collections/*%2B*', '/collections/*filter*&*filter*', '/*?*ls=*&ls=*', '/*?*oseid=*', '/*?*preview_theme_id=*', '/*?*preview_script*'. No Crawl-delay. I requested NONE of those: every collection URL was the bare /collections/ form, and the only query string used anywhere was the plain '?page=N' pagination parameter (not covered by any Disallow) during the mirror-overlap enumeration, plus Shopify's own from=/to= sitemap params. Shopify's header steers agents to a UCP/MCP endpoint; that is a commerce/checkout channel and was NOT used - everything below is ordinary server-rendered HTML. ACCESS: clean. probe.fetch() returned HTTP 200 on the first or second fingerprint every time (chrome124, safari15_5, safari18_0_ios); no bot wall, no challenge, no 403, no 429. 2s per-host pacing left in force. TREE: taken from Seletti's OWN mega-menu, which is fully server-rendered in the homepage HTML, and cross-checked against its OWN collections sitemap. Top-level departments: Tableware, Lighting, Furniture, Objects, Outdoor, plus designer-collab and price/gift entries. THERE IS NO BATHROOM / BAGNO DEPARTMENT. The bathroom finding is one leaf inside OBJECTS. The full Objects child list, verbatim from the menu, is: Art Toy, Candles, Candleholders, Cases, Dustbin, Flower Holder - Vases, Home accessories, Letters, Mats, Mirrors, Notebooks, Photo frames, SOAP DISH, Smoke Tray, Terracotta, Thermal Bottles, Travel, Textiles. 'Soap Dish' is a genuine product-type nav node - Seletti's menu labels several nodes by product type while pointing them at a designer-collab collection handle (the same pattern gives 'Textiles' -> /collections/dondi-x-seletti). I verified the label is not an English-only accident: the Italian storefront at https://www.seletti.it/it/ carries the node-for-node identical menu with the label 'PORTASAPONE' pointing at /it/collections/brain-wash-seletti-x-propaganda. A keyword sweep of the IT homepage HTML for 'bagno' returns ZERO hits, so there is no Bagno / Accessori bagno node to walk. NOT STOPPING AT THE MENU (BATCH_BRIEF s5 - orphan collections): I read the full collections sitemap https://www.seletti.it/sitemap_collections_1.xml?from=612230725979&to=679452508507 (HTTP 200), which enumerates ALL 161 collections on the storefront, and grepped every handle for bath/bagno/soap/sapon/shower/doccia/toothbrush/spazzol/towel/asciugam/toilet/carta-igien/mirror/specchi/wash/lavabo/basin/sink/rubinett/faucet/bidet/wc/vasca/portasapone/dispenser/holder. There is NO bathroom collection at any depth, orphan or otherwise; the only hits were the four mirror collections handled in review[] and the collab handle 'toiletpaper-home-1' (the Toiletpaper magazine art collaboration - a NAME, not toilet paper: rule 2, do not classify on a word). I also read the products sitemaps (sitemap_products_1 + _2, 1,670 products in total) and ran the same sweep at PRODUCT level, which is the strongest possible evidence of what Seletti actually sells: soap -> 7 hits, of which the only bathroom objects are brain-wash-white / brain-wash-black (both captured by the recorded node) and the rest are enamel plates/mugs printed 'soap', a Toiletpaper Beauty soap kit and soap bars; shower -> 2 hits, 'toiletpaper-beauty-shower-gel' (a cosmetic) and 'aquart-shower'; bath -> 7 hits, six Toiletpaper PETS bath mats and 'supershelf-bathroom-blue-grid'; toothbrush/towel rail/toilet roll holder/basin/tap/bidet/WC/vasca -> ZERO. For the four orphan mirror collections I enumerated every page (16 tiles/page) and compared handle sets, which is how the subset findings in review[] were proved. Nothing is estimated, inferred from a parent, or summed from siblings; no product API was used. WHAT THE RECORDED NODE CONTAINS AND WHY IT IS BATHROOM (rules 2, 13, 18): the node's own name in both locales is a bathroom accessory type (Soap Dish / Portasapone). Its 4 products are the Brain Wash pieces by Propaganda x Seletti: 'Brain wash - White' and 'Brain wash - Black', whose own JSON-LD description reads 'Soap Holder + Soap' (SKU 13501, cm 15 x 11 x 7.5) - i.e. soap dishes/holders, squarely rule 13 'Soap Dispensers/Dishes/Holders' and rule 18 - plus two Brain wash soap-bar refills for the same holder. DISCLOSED: 2 of the 4 are the soap bars themselves, which are consumables rather than accessories; the qty 4 is the listing page's OWN total and rule 26 forbids adjusting it, so it is recorded verbatim with the composition stated here. Primary product type of the node is a soap dish, so it goes to Bathroom, not to Decor. NO OTHER BATHROOM NODE EXISTS: there is no bath, shower, enclosure, tap, basin, toilet, bidet, vanity, bathroom cabinet, bathroom storage, towel rail, toilet-roll holder or toothbrush holder category anywhere on the site. The one shower-shaped item, 'Aquart Shower' (/products/aquart-shower), is a single PRODUCT with JSON-LD category 'Objects' and a description that begins 'Who said that you have to take a shower in the bathroom? ... Do it outdoors' - a concrete-and-copper 220cm GARDEN shower. It has no category node of its own, and rules 24/27 forbid recording a product-detail URL, so it is not recorded; noted here so it is not silently skipped. Likewise 'SUPERSHELF BATHROOM BLUE GRID' is a single Superfurniture shelf whose own JSON-LD category is 'Furniture'. DEDUP: already_extracted() was run on every candidate leaf and every review node. Hard hits: small-mirrors (Final.xlsx 'Mirrors') and wall-mirrors (Final.xlsx 'Wall Mirrors') - both banked in review[], never in rows[]. The recorded Soap Dish URL returns None, and so does its /it/ form. Locale blind spots (b) and (c) checked, not assumed: the PDP and PLP hreflang blocks list exactly three alternates - x-default, en and it - ALL on www.seletti.it (e.g. x-default/en https://www.seletti.it/collections/brain-wash-seletti-x-propaganda, it https://www.seletti.it/it/collections/brain-wash-seletti-x-propaganda). There is no separate country domain, so there is no cross-HOST alternate that could be hiding in the index; and all 41 Seletti URLs already in Furniture.xlsx and Final.xlsx are on the bare EN path form, matching what I checked. rel=canonical on the recorded leaf is self-canonical. EXCLUDED AND WHY: Lighting and its 7 children (rule 19; 5 already in Final.xlsx); Tableware and its 11 children (Kitchen & Dining, already in Final.xlsx); Furniture and its 20 children (Furniture.xlsx); Vases/Candles/Candleholders/Home accessories/Letters/Photo frames/Art Toy (rule 21 Decor, already in Final.xlsx); Curtains and Cushions (rule 20 Textile); Outdoor, Pets, Jewelry, Sunglasses, Spare Parts (out of scope); Christmas, Black Friday, gift-guide, price-band, New Arrival, Best Seller, Sales and the ~60 designer/series collections (rule 25 promotional). Mats, Cases, Beauty and Dustbin were each opened and inspected rather than dismissed by name - see review[]. CONCLUSION: Seletti is an Italian design brand with no bathroom department, but it does merchandise one explicit bathroom-accessory node, 'Soap Dish' / 'Portasapone' (4 products), which is recorded. Everything else that touches bathroom territory is either already extracted, an orphan subset of an already-extracted node, or a non-bathroom node, and is banked in review[]. This is NOT a robots exclusion and NOT an access block - robots.txt names no Claude agent and every request returned HTTP 200.
